conditions.label: Secondary malignant neoplasm of adrenal gland
conditions.note: Bilateral adrenal metastases from breast cancer.

reports.text: Sinus tachycardia, rate 101. Normal axis. PR, QRS and QT intervals normal. No ST or T-wave changes. No peaked T waves.

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text:
CT abdomen and pelvis with IV contrast.
Comparison: 09/02/2025.
Adrenal glands: new bilateral adrenal masses, right 3.6 cm and left 4.1 cm, heterogeneously enhancing, not present on the prior study.
Liver: known hepatic metastases remain, smaller than on 05/06/2025; no new liver lesion.
Pancreas, spleen, kidneys: unremarkable. No lymphadenopathy. No ascites.
Pelvis: post-hysterectomy, unremarkable.
Bones: no suspicious lesion.
reports.conclusion: New bilateral adrenal masses, consistent with metastases. Treated hepatic metastases without new liver disease.

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Emergency Department - Physician Record
Date of service: 02/27/2026, arrival 07:10 by ambulance
Patient: Janet Madden, 60F

CC: passed out at home this morning.

HPI: 60-year-old woman with metastatic ER+ breast cancer to the liver on letrozole and palbociclib. Weeks of worsening tiredness and lightheadedness on standing; this morning she stood up from the kitchen table, felt the room go gray and woke on the floor, no injury, no incontinence, no tongue biting, back to herself within a minute. She has been craving salt - salting everything, eating pickles from the jar. About 10 lb lost over the past two months. No chest pain, palpitations, fever, vomiting, diarrhea or bleeding.

Meds (per patient and pharmacy list): letrozole 2.5 mg daily, palbociclib 125 mg days 1-21, escitalopram 10 mg, oxycodone/acetaminophen 5/325 PRN, polyethylene glycol PRN, ibuprofen PRN, calcium/vitamin D, multivitamin. Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: BP 90/60 supine, HR 102. Orthostatic: symptomatic with a fall in pressure on standing, test stopped. Thin, tired. Skin hyperpigmented, darkest in the palmar creases and the mastectomy and laparoscopic scars. Heart tachycardic, regular. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, mild RUQ tenderness. No focal neurologic deficit. No head injury.

Results: Na 128, K 5.5, Cl 95, HCO3 24, BUN 18, Cr 0.9, glucose 65. 08:00 cortisol 3. Cosyntropin 250 mcg IV at 08:05; 60-minute cortisol 5. ACTH (drawn with the baseline cortisol) 486, resulted later in the day. ECG sinus tachycardia, no hyperkalemic changes. CT A/P: new bilateral adrenal masses (R 3.6 cm, L 4.1 cm) consistent with metastases; liver lesions smaller than in May.

ED course: D50 25 mL for glucose 65, then dextrose-containing saline. 2 L normal saline. Hydrocortisone 100 mg IV after the stimulation sample. BP 108/68, HR 84 by 12:30; dizziness improved.

Impression:
1. Adrenal insufficiency, primary, from bilateral adrenal metastases - adrenal crisis presentation.
2. Syncope due to #1.
3. Hyponatremia, hyperkalemia, hypoglycemia due to #1.
4. Metastatic breast cancer with new adrenal involvement.

Disposition: admitted to medicine.

Emergency Medicine

medications.sig: Take 3 tablets (15 mg) on waking and 1 tablet (5 mg) at 2 PM. Double or triple doses on sick days as instructed.
Inject 100 mg into the thigh muscle once for vomiting, collapse or inability to take oral hydrocortisone, then call 911

procedures.procedure: Hospital discharge day management, 30 minutes or less

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
Discharge Summary - Hospital Medicine
Admitted 02/27/2026, discharged 03/02/2026

Principal diagnosis: adrenal crisis due to primary adrenal insufficiency from bilateral adrenal metastases.
Other: metastatic ER+/HER2- breast cancer (liver, now adrenals); depression; chemotherapy-induced neuropathy; osteopenia.

Hospital course: Admitted from the ED after syncope with hypotension, hyponatremia, hyperkalemia and hypoglycemia; 08:00 cortisol 3 with a 60-minute post-cosyntropin cortisol of 5 and ACTH 486, confirming primary adrenal insufficiency. CT showed new bilateral adrenal masses. Treated with hydrocortisone 50 mg IV every 6 hours and IV fluids, tapered to oral hydrocortisone on day 3, with fludrocortisone added for mineralocorticoid replacement. Orthostatic symptoms resolved and she walked the unit independently. Sodium 134 and potassium 4.6 on the day of discharge; glucose normal throughout after day 1. Endocrinology saw her in hospital and will follow as an outpatient. Oncology informed of new adrenal disease.

Discharge medications:
NEW hydrocortisone 15 mg on waking and 5 mg at 2 PM
NEW fludrocortisone 0.1 mg daily
NEW hydrocortisone sodium succinate 100 mg IM emergency kit (taught to self-inject)
CONTINUE letrozole 2.5 mg daily and palbociclib 125 mg days 1-21 pending oncology review; escitalopram 10 mg daily; oxycodone/acetaminophen 5/325 PRN; polyethylene glycol PRN; ibuprofen PRN; calcium/vitamin D; multivitamin.

Patient education: sick-day rules (double the hydrocortisone dose for fever or illness; triple for severe illness; injection and 911 if vomiting), medical alert ID, wallet steroid card provided.

Follow-up: PCP within 1 week; endocrinology 2 weeks; oncology 2-3 weeks. BMP at PCP visit.
Condition at discharge: good. Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Transitional care outreach
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Post-discharge call (d/c 3/2, adrenal crisis). Pt home, says she feels 'like a person again'. No dizziness standing, eating and drinking well. Picked up hydrocortisone, fludrocortisone and the injection kit yesterday; reviewed timing 15 mg on waking / 5 mg at 2 pm. Reviewed sick-day doubling and when to use the shot. Has endo appt 3/12. TCM visit booked Thu 3/5 with PCP; BMP that day.

documents.title: Transitional Care Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TCM visit. Admitted 2/27-3/2 after syncope at home: adrenal crisis from primary adrenal insufficiency, new bilateral adrenal mets on CT. Discharge summary and ED record reviewed in full.

Now: energy much better, no lightheadedness, salt craving gone, appetite good. Taking hydrocortisone 15 on waking / 5 at 2 pm and fludrocortisone 0.1 daily, alarms on her phone. Kit in her purse. Wearing a medical alert bracelet.
Meds reconciled: hydrocortisone, fludrocortisone, IM hydrocortisone kit, letrozole, palbociclib (onc to review), escitalopram 10, oxycodone/APAP prn, PEG prn, ibuprofen prn, Ca/D, MVI.

Exam: BP normal, no orthostatic drop sitting to standing. Wt 58.8. Skin still darker in creases and scars. Heart regular, lungs clear, mild RUQ tenderness, no edema.

BMP today: Na 137, K 4.3.

A/P
1. Primary adrenal insufficiency (adrenal mets) - stable on replacement. Sick-day rules reviewed again with teach-back; she lives alone, so asked her to tell a neighbor where the kit is. Endo 3/12.
2. Metastatic breast ca, new adrenal progression - oncology appt pending.
3. Weight 58.8, recheck in 2 months.
4. Tdap due this year - at next visit.
RTC 2 months.

documents.title: Endocrinology consultation
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Endocrinology - Outpatient Consultation (03/12/2026)

Dear colleague,

I saw Ms. Madden after her admission for adrenal crisis. The biochemistry - low 08:00 cortisol of 3, flat response to cosyntropin (5 at 60 minutes), ACTH 486, potassium 5.5 with hyponatremia - together with the new bilateral adrenal metastases establishes primary adrenal insufficiency from metastatic replacement of both glands.

She is well on hydrocortisone 15 mg on waking and 5 mg at 2 pm with fludrocortisone 0.1 mg daily. Seated blood pressure normal without postural drop. Sodium and potassium normal at her PCP visit.

Recommendations: continue current doses; adjust fludrocortisone by blood pressure, postural symptoms and potassium. Sick-day rules reinforced. Injection technique reviewed with a trainer device. Stress-dose coverage for procedures and any future surgery. Return in 3 months with BMP.

Endocrinology

medications.sig: 500 mg (two 250 mg injections) IM on days 1, 15 and 29, then every 28 days, given in oncology clinic

documents.title: Medical oncology visit
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
Medical Oncology - Clinic Note
Date of service: 03/17/2026

Dx: Metastatic breast carcinoma, ER+/HER2-, liver (05/2025) and now bilateral adrenal glands (02/2026), with primary adrenal insufficiency.

Interval: hospitalized 02/27-03/02 with adrenal crisis; doing well on hydrocortisone/fludrocortisone. CT 02/27 shows new bilateral adrenal masses while the liver lesions continued to shrink - progression on letrozole/palbociclib after about 9 months.

Plan:
- Stop letrozole and palbociclib.
- Start fulvestrant 500 mg IM days 1, 15, 29 then every 28 days; first dose given today. Stress dosing not required for injections.
- Restaging CT in 3 months.
- Continue pain regimen.

Medical Oncology

events.reason: Question about dental visit and refill

documents.title: Dentist and refill
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Two things: I have a routine cleaning next week - do I need to take extra hydrocortisone for that? And I'm down to 10 days of the fludrocortisone, the hospital only gave me one month. Can you send it to my usual pharmacy?

documents.title: RE: Dentist and refill
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Janet - for a routine cleaning you don't need extra. If you ever need an extraction or anything under numbing that is more than a quick filling, check with endocrinology first; they may want a one-time extra dose. Fludrocortisone 0.1 mg daily, 90 days with refills, sent to your pharmacy. I sent the hydrocortisone too so they line up.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
2-month f/u.
Adrenal insufficiency: hydrocortisone 15/5, fludro 0.1. No dizziness, no salt craving, no sick days so far. Endo happy.
Onc: fulvestrant since 3/17, injections monthly now; tolerating, mild soreness at injection sites. Restaging CT next month.
Pain 3/10, oxycodone/APAP a few times a week.
Mood: PHQ-9 6. Garden is going in. Continues escitalopram 10; counseling monthly.
Neuropathy unchanged.
Wt 60.5 (58.8 in March).

Exam: BP normal sitting and standing. Skin creases less dark. Heart/lungs normal. Abd soft, minimal RUQ tenderness. No edema.

A/P
1. Primary adrenal insufficiency - stable. BMP today.
2. Metastatic ER+ breast ca on fulvestrant - per onc.
3. MDD recurrent - stable.
4. Tdap given today (last 2016).
RTC September, flu shot then.

documents.title: Immunization
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Tdap 0.5 mL IM L deltoid. VIS given. No reaction.

documents.title: Endocrinology follow-up
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body: Endocrinology follow-up (06/11/2026): Doing well on hydrocortisone 15 mg/5 mg and fludrocortisone 0.1 mg. BP normal without postural drop; recent BMP normal. No change. Return in 6 months.
